summary: Kootenai National Forest lookout about 19 miles northwest of Libby, MT: wooden L-4 tower built 1934, listed as gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association and firelookout.com; no removal date in the sources read.

access.note: Summit area is along the public Skyline Trail on Kootenai National Forest land; no source describes the lookout site itself.

visit.trail_note: The Skyline Trail runs near the summit; from the trail, go about 1,000 feet north to the south shoulder for a view.

events.note: Listed as a wooden L-4 tower at 10 feet; the listing does not say whether 10 feet is the height

evidence.supports: built 1934 as a wooden L-4 design; the 10-foot figure is given without a stated meaning
status gone, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association list
trail passes near the summit; view from the south shoulder about 1,000 feet north of the trail
evidence.quote: At Arbo Mountain summit, hike about 1000' north of the trail to reach the south shoulder, viewing the Mule Creek/Seventeen Mile Creek drainages and mountains to the northeast.

evidence.supports: trail and lookouts on Arbo, Skyline and Quartz mountains built for fire suppression (listing wording is garbled)
evidence.quote: The trail and lookouts were at Arbo, Skyline, and Quartz Mountains were constructed for fire suppression

evidence.supports: Skyline Trail is part of the National Recreation Trail System
evidence.quote: The Skyline Trail System is part of the National Recreation Trail System

notes_for_editor: Only firelookout.com gives a build year and dimensions; the FFLA list gives only the status Tower Gone. The 10-foot figure may be a cab or platform size rather than tower height, so height_m is left out and the story says the listing does not explain the figure. No removal date was found. The Skyline Trail listing has a garbled sentence about lookouts on Arbo, Skyline and Quartz mountains; the story paraphrases it cautiously and the quote is kept verbatim. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the firelookout page does not place the lookout on the summit, so the story says Arbo Mountain instead. Searches run: 2. Not yet checked: Libby newspaper coverage and the Northwest Montana Lookout Association, which may hold removal details.
